Please review; Evelyn you're the owner for responsibility wording and any legal caveats. Once we align I'll produce a formatted PDF for Jordan's SIG.

--- Draft answers (network/security architecture) ---
1) VPC peering:
- Hosted API: We do not support direct VPC peering into customer VPCs for the multi-tenant Hosted offering. Customers use HTTPS over the public internet or PrivateLink (see below) to avoid public exposure.
- Dedicated/Private: VPC peering is supported for our Dedicated and Private deployments when the customer runs in a dedicated account or via our Private deployment model. We require non-overlapping CIDRs; route tables must allow routing to Redwood subnets. Cross-account peering is supported with our standard peering acceptance workflow; customers must provide CIDR ranges and a designated network contact.

2) Private endpoints / PrivateLink:
- We support AWS PrivateLink (NLB + VPC endpoint services) for Hosted (via customer-managed VPC endpoints) and for Dedicated/Private we can provision PrivateLink endpoints into the customer's VPC on request.
- Azure Private Endpoint is supported for Private deployments; Azure customers can request a private endpoint configuration during provisioning.
- Regions: PrivateLink support is available in our primary regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). For other regions, provisioning may require a short lead time.

3) Hosted API egress IPs & allowlisting:
- We publish a set of static egress CIDRs used for API responses and callbacks in ip_allowlist_ranges.csv. These ranges are stable; changes are announced at least 14 days in advance and published in our changelog and status page.
- Note: certain edge/third-party CDN IPs may be outside these ranges during failover. Customers requiring absolute static IPs should use PrivateLink or our Dedicated offering.

4) Dedicated / Private egress patterns:
- Customers can bring their own NAT or use our managed NAT in Dedicated/Private installations. BYO NAT/egress IP is supported when we have routing configured in the customer's account. Recommended pattern: customer-managed NAT with explicit routing to Redwood subnets for full control over egress auditing.

5) Ports/protocols:
- Ingress to Redwood-hosted APIs: TCP 443 (HTTPS) only. We terminate TLS at our edge.
- Health checks (if peering or private endpoints are used): TCP 443 and optional TCP 80 for legacy health endpoints (rare).
- Inter-service: internal ports use TLS and mutual authentication; customers do not need to open these unless running private/on-prem integrations.

6) Diagrams/artifacts: attached: redwood_network_diagram_v2.pdf (overview: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, peering and PrivateLink flows); ip_allowlist_ranges.csv (current CIDRs); also producing sig_answers_network_section.pdf for direct upload to your SIG portal.

Caveats / security notes:
- For Hosted customers using public endpoints we recommend IP allowlisting + mTLS via our API gateway for extra trust, and using API keys scoped to route-level policies.
- VPC peering requires explicit routing and does not provide Google-level load balancing — customers should plan for cross-AZ routing and route propagation.

If this looks good I will (a) export the network section to the SIG template, (b) sign the attestation page, and (c) upload the artifacts.
